description: Shared split fixtures for the Rust engine (cargo test) and the JS engine (npm test). Defaults per case: useRegex=false, trimParts=false, keepEmptyLines=true. 'expected' applies to both engines; a case with a known engine difference uses 'expectedRust' + 'expectedJs' and must explain it in 'divergence' ('resolved' documents a former divergence). Rows are the data lines of the shared line model (Paket 6, tests/fixtures/line-endings-cases.json): LF, CRLF and CR are line breaks, a trailing line break adds no row, an empty text has no rows. Every expected result is column-major: expected[column][row]. Paket 10 Phase B: 'delimiter' is a string or { repeat, count }; an expectation can also be { error: invalidRegex }; 'divergence' is a string (accepted dialect difference) or { kind, reason } with kind dialect | utf16Damage (the JS split puts a split position inside a surrogate pair, R2) | unvalidatedInput; 'ref' is a finding of docs/analyse/Paket10-PhaseA-Regex-Analyse.md. The expectations describe the CURRENT behaviour. A not yet implemented decision of Paket 10 (docs/analyse/Paket10-PhaseB-Regexvertrag.md) is stated as 'target' (both engines) or 'targetRust' + 'targetJs': the columns or { error: invalidRegex | emptyDelimiter | emptyPattern | patternTooLong | regexSplitsCharacter (JS only) }, together with 'pending' { decisions, phase, engines, reason }: exactly the engines listed in 'engines' still differ from their target (checked by both runners against the real engines).

cases.name: R2/E5: regex matching the high surrogate

divergence.reason: The JS match removes the high half of the emoji, the low half stays alone in the next column. fancy-regex rejects \uD83D.

pending.reason: A match that ends inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS.

cases.name: R2/E5: regex matching the low surrogate

divergence.reason: The JS match removes the low half of the emoji, the high half stays alone in the first column. fancy-regex rejects \uDE00.

pending.reason: A match that starts inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS.

cases.name: R2/E5: character class with an emoji matches both halves as two adjacent delimiters

divergence.reason: Without the u flag [😀] is the class of the two code units: two adjacent matches split inside the emoji and create an empty column that exists only between the halves.

pending.reason: Every split position counts, also between two adjacent matches: a position inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS.

cases.name: R2/E5: character class with an emoji on another emoji with the same high surrogate

divergence.reason: The JS class matches the shared high half of 😁 (U+1F601): the low half stays alone. fancy-regex does not match 😁 at all.

pending.reason: A match that ends inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS.

cases.name: R2/E5: capture group with a class of the halves

divergence.reason: JS split inserts every capture as a column: each half of the emoji becomes its own column (lone surrogates). fancy-regex drops captures (dialect).

pending.reason: Split positions inside a surrogate pair are refused in JS, also when the match is captured.

cases.name: R2/E5: capture group around the high surrogate

divergence.reason: The captured high half and the remaining low half land in different columns. fancy-regex rejects \uD83D.

pending.reason: A split position inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS, also when the match is captured.

cases.name: R2/E5: capture group around a whole emoji is a dialect difference only
cases.divergence: Capture groups: fancy-regex split drops captured text, JS split inserts the capture as an extra column. The emoji stays whole.

cases.name: R2/E5: capture of the high surrogate inside a match of the whole emoji

divergence.reason: The whole match is the emoji (its start and end are character boundaries), but JS split inserts the capture, which ends inside the surrogate pair: the column holds a lone high surrogate. fancy-regex rejects \uD83D.

pending.reason: A capture boundary inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS, even if the whole match is safe.

cases.name: R2/E5: capture of the low surrogate inside a match of the whole emoji

divergence.reason: The whole match is the emoji, but the inserted capture starts inside the surrogate pair: the column holds a lone low surrogate. fancy-regex rejects \uD83D.

pending.reason: A capture boundary inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS, even if the whole match is safe.

cases.name: R2/E5: two captures split the halves of a match of the whole emoji

divergence.reason: The whole match is the emoji, but the two inserted captures put its halves into two columns (lone surrogates). fancy-regex rejects \uD83D.

pending.reason: Capture boundaries inside a surrogate pair are refused in JS, even if the whole match is safe.

cases.name: R2/E5: two captures of whole emoji are a dialect difference only
cases.divergence: Capture groups: fancy-regex split drops captured text, JS split inserts each capture as an extra column. Every capture holds whole characters.

cases.name: R2/E5: dot as delimiter on an emoji

divergence.reason: JS . matches each code unit: the split position between the two halves adds a column although no value contains a lone surrogate.

pending.reason: The split positions decide, not only the values: a position inside a surrogate pair is refused in JS.

cases.name: R2/E5: cut emoji in several rows with different line endings

divergence.reason: In every row with an emoji the JS class matches both halves separately and adds a column between them; the line endings (CRLF, CR) are not affected.

pending.reason: One cut row refuses the whole split (no partial result).

cases.name: R5/E3: empty regex pattern

divergence.reason: Neither the JS worker nor Rust checks the empty pattern: both split between every character (with the usual empty parts in Rust). Only SplitPage and the main-thread path refuse it.

pending.reason: An empty regex pattern is refused with its own error in the worker and in Rust.

R7/E9: $ before U+2028 inside a line (JS flag m)
cases.divergence: JS split uses the flags gm: with m, $ also matches before U+2028/U+2029 inside a line. fancy-regex $ only matches at the end of the line (and yields an empty part there).

pending.reason: With the flag g only, $ matches only at the end of the line; the remaining difference is the empty part after an empty match at the end (dialect).

cases.name: R7/E9: ^ after U+2028 inside a line (JS flag m)
cases.divergence: JS split uses the flags gm: with m, ^ also matches after U+2028/U+2029. fancy-regex ^ only matches at the start of the line (and yields an empty part before it).

pending.reason: With the flag g only, ^ matches only at the start of the line; the remaining difference is the empty part before an empty match at the start (dialect).

cases.name: R7/E9: ^b after U+2029 inside a line (JS flag m)
cases.divergence: JS split uses the flags gm: with m, U+2029 starts a new line for ^. fancy-regex does not match.

pending.reason: With the flag g only, both engines agree.

cases.name: R7/E9: a$ before U+2028 inside a line (JS flag m)
cases.divergence: JS split uses the flags gm: with m, a$ matches before U+2028. fancy-regex does not match (the JS Filter, flag g, does not match either).

pending.reason: With the flag g only, both engines agree.

cases.name: R7/E9: $ at the end of CRLF lines is not affected by the flag m
